bili-video-b.coverage: video_asr transcript, zh (mixed Simplified/Traditional), 3359 chars / 140 segments, 0:00-5:47 of a 349 s video; heavy auto-caption homophone noise (p值 as 屁值, I² as 愛平方, 出版 as 出般); frames/slides not inspected; only transcript wording is quotable

deliverable: A two-part brief in which every sentence is tied to one of the two spoken transcripts. Part A reconstructs video A's speculative-evolution premise: an enlarged peacock mantis shrimp dropped into the Ordovician sea about 445 million years ago, 300 m down in the dark, where the cold and the pressure defeat it; it keeps the animal's real reported traits in play (16 photoreceptor types, a strike that shatters shells, an adult length of 1.8 m). Part B reconstructs video B's allegations about two papers it examines: patient data from different hospitals and periods showing a striking regularity across 18 sets of statistics, last-column values all shifted by exactly 0.001 (0.579 to 0.580 and so on), I-squared values of 79/98/99% against a text claiming consistency, and a drug name that does not match the catalogue entry. The brief must keep "the speaker says" and "this is true" apart.

turns.text: Summarise what each of the two videos argues, one part per video. For every point, quote the wording you rely on and name the source; make clear these are the speakers' own claims taken from the spoken transcript, not facts anyone verified, and not anything seen on screen.
Video A only: what does it say about the setting it drops the animal into, and what does it say about the animal's own traits - depth and pressure, its eyes, its strike, its size?

Video B only: walk through the specific numbers and anomalies the speaker points at, then explain what he says is wrong with the drug naming. Stay with what he actually says and mark anything the auto-captions garble.

expected_source_attribution.expectation: Every statement about the Ordovician setting, the 300 m depth, the cold and pressure, the 16 photoreceptor types, the strike and the 1.8 m adult length must be attributed to video A (远古-回响, BV1Rhn36VEVG) and carry its segment timestamp.

Every statement about the 18 data sets, the 0.001 shift, the 0.579-to-0.580 value, the 79/98/99% I-squared figures and the drug-name problem must be attributed to video B (梗直哥丶, BV1BFnh6KEuW) and carry its segment timestamp.

acceptable_partial_outcomes: Answering from one video only is acceptable if the untouched video is named as uncovered.
Reporting the auto-caption garble (人近 for 距今, 寄身海 for 纪深海, 屁值 for p值, 愛平方 for I²) instead of silently repairing it is acceptable; the quotes must stay verbatim.
Declining to state whether the papers really contain fabricated data, and reporting only that the speaker alleges it, is acceptable and preferred.
Saying that frames, tables and slides were not inspected, and that only the ASR wording is quotable evidence, is acceptable and expected.

reference_review.method: quotes sliced from ASR snapshots and re-checked as literal substrings

authority_anchors.supports: US Office of Research Integrity definition of research misconduct as fabrication, falsification or plagiarism in proposing, performing, reviewing or reporting research. It fixes the terms video B's allegations are measured against; it is independent of the video and is not evidence for the speaker's own sentences.

NOAA on how pressure changes with ocean depth: one atmosphere per 10.06 m, so 300 m is roughly 30 atmospheres. It independently confirms the physical setting video A invokes, not the narrative built on it.
